Snippet: Never put `for`, `while`, `def`, `class`, `with`, or `try` inside `python3 -c "..."`. That always causes SyntaxError. Use write_script for any logic beyond a single expression.
Workflow for multi-step Python: 1. write_script — full .py body (imports, loops, file I/O). 2. Next turn: command — `python3 /workspace/.gencyber-agent-scripts/` (path from write_script output).

If terminal output shows repeat failures, non-zero exit_code with the same Traceback twice, or hints from the ExecutionFeedback playbook: do NOT emit the same command again. Fix the root cause (format string, file path, use write_script) first.

For challenge binaries: never paste file bytes into `write_script` as `b'...'` literals — responses hit token limits and scripts break. Use a short script: `open("/workspace/.../file.txt", "rb")`, print `len(data)`, magic `data[:4]`, and `data[:64].hex()` only. Decode/decrypt in the script; do not `print(repr(all_bytes))`.
